identity.real_world_identity_notes: FIA material establishes six manual ratios for the Storm family, and a documented Storm GTM uses a Hewland TGTA six-speed sequential push-pull lever. AMS2 visibly models the sequential lever without paddles.

wheel_rim.notes: Direct cockpit inspection showed a D-shaped rim without an integrated display; exact diameter remains unknown.

notes: With Auto Clutch disabled, the car stalled when moving from rest without physical clutch input.
All six sequential-stick gears accepted clutch-free full-throttle upshifts with perceptible automatic cut.
Clutch-free downshifts were accepted and no automatic throttle blip was observed; authentic rev matching therefore requires the driver to blip the throttle manually.
The opened historical hardware sources do not prove that every late Storm GTM used the same exact gearbox specification.
Live-tested in AMS2 1.6.9.91 with Auto Clutch disabled.
Standing-start clutch, six-speed sequential stick, automatic cut, no automatic blip, and the D-shaped no-display rim were directly observed.

confidence.basis: Exact simulator identity and behavior were directly tested; FIA and specialist chassis evidence independently support the six-speed sequential-stick hardware family. Manual blipping is the driver-supplied rev-matching technique for the verified non-auto-blip downshift behavior.

claims.basis: Official release plus exact live CarModel and GT1_05 class observation.
Historical sources and direct observation agree on six-speed sequential lever hardware, while the exact chassis mapping remains qualified.

Direct current-game tests and cockpit inspection establish clutch-free sequential downshifts with no automatic blip; manual throttle blipping is therefore the required authentic driver-supplied rev-matching technique.
